items.content_html:
Summary

Add compatibility data for FontFace.sizeAdjust, the JavaScript property corresponding to the @font-face size-adjust descriptor. Record Chrome 92, Firefox 92, and Safari 17, with derived browsers mirrored.

Test results and supporting details

  • npm test passed: formatting/type checks, data lint, and all 347 unit tests.
  • Reviewed the final diff separately and checked implementation/release evidence:
    • Chromium 92 FontFace IDL gates the property on CSSFontFaceSizeAdjust. The flag changes from test in 91 to stable in 92.
    • Gecko bug 1698495 includes the WebIDL implementation; the shipping announcement identifies Firefox 92 as the default-enabled release.
    • WebKit implementation commit adds the FontFace property and constructor descriptor and enables the shared feature flag. Safari 17 release notes confirm the shipping release.
  • The current specification includes sizeAdjust in FontFace's IDL, but has no dedicated property anchor, so this links to the interface section.
  • Omit mdn_url until the accompanying reference page is published.

Related issues

Related to mdn/content#36587. This is the BCD-first change requested in mdn/content#36587 (comment); documentation follows separately.
items.title: Add FontFace.sizeAdjust compatibility data

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds a Safari note to css.at-rules.media.forced-colors: forced-colors: active is never true, as Apple platforms have no forced colors mode, and the feature always matches forced-colors: none. Safari on iOS inherits it through mirror. Same shape as the display-mode: minimal-ui notes in the same file.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit implemented the feature as a placeholder that always matches none because Cocoa has no forced colors concept: bug 225281, landed as 253290@main for Safari 16. The issue reporter confirmed that Increase Contrast on macOS does not apply rules inside @media (forced-colors: active).

Chrome Android and Firefox Android, raised in the issue, are left out: their behaviour was not verified here and can follow in a separate PR.

node lint/lint.js css/at-rules/media.json: all data passed linting.

Related issues

Fixes #27143
items.title: Note that forced-colors: active is never true in Safari

Adds css.at-rules.view-transition.navigation and css.at-rules.view-transition.types, the two descriptors of the @view-transition rule, with the same support as the at-rule: Chrome 126, Safari 18.2, Firefox unsupported, the rest mirrored. The entries follow the shape of other at-rule descriptors such as @property and carry no mdn_url, since MDN has no page for either descriptor yet.

Test results and supporting details

Chromium: @view-transition parses only when ViewTransitionOnNavigation is enabled, stable in 126 (chromestatus); types was already in CSSViewTransitionRule.idl at 126.0.6478.0.

WPT: css/css-view-transitions/navigation/at-rule-opt-in-auto.html and css/css-view-transitions/navigation/with-types/at-rule-with-types-parsing.html.

items.content_html:
Summary

Sets Safari support for css.properties.letter-spacing.percentages and css.properties.word-spacing.percentages to 17.4 instead of 7, and Firefox support for css.properties.letter-spacing.percentages to 133 instead of 45. Safari on iOS and Firefox for Android mirror. Firefox stays at 45 for word-spacing, which got percentages in a separate, earlier bug.

Test results and supporting details

Safari: WebKit bug 262762, "Implement percentage values for letter-spacing and word-spacing [css-text-4]", was fixed on 2023-11-30 by WebKit PR 18771 (271357@main), which added percentage support to both properties in one commit. The post WebKit Features in Safari 17.4 lists it under "Percentages in spacing": "WebKit for Safari 17.4 adds support for percentages in letter-spacing and word-spacing." Before that commit WebKit's grammar accepted only <length> for either property, so no earlier Safari parsed a percentage.

Firefox: bug 1884118 made letter-spacing accept <length-percentage> (94d220f04c1c), with target milestone 133 and status-firefox133: fixed. word-spacing percentages landed in bug 1038663, fixed in Firefox 45, so that entry is already right. Thanks to @caugner for the source tree research in the issue that pinned 133.

node lint/lint.js on both files: all data passed linting.

Related issues

Fixes #30826
items.title: Correct Safari/Firefox for `{letter,word}-spacing` percentages

items.content_html:
…relList, and referrerPolicy properties

Summary

Firefox Nightly 159 adds support for the MathMLAnchorElement download, ping, rel, relList, and referrerPolicy properties; see https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2064612.

This PR adds data points for these new properties.

Note that the spec URL situation is a bit odd — the impl bug points to https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-a-element for the spec, which I guess isn't totally unreasonable, as download, ping, rel, and referrerPolicy at least are just reflected properties.

I couldn't find a spec URL of any kind for relList, so I've just marked that as non-standard for now.

Test results and supporting details

I tested all of these, and verified that they worked in Nightly 159. I viewed the example at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MathMLAnchorElement#examples in the MDN Playground. I updated the first link to include these attributes:

download="yes"
ping="https://example-tracking.com https://example-analytics.com"
rel="help alternate"
referrerPolicy="no-referrer"

Then I added the following code to access the new properties:

outputValue("download");
outputValue("ping");
outputValue("rel");
console.log(mathAnchor.relList[0]);
outputValue("referrerPolicy");

Related issues
items.title: Firefox preview support for MathMLAnchorElement download, ping, rel, …

Summary

To avoid a ranged Baseline date in web-features, reconcile the dir data with api.HTMLElement.dir.

Test results and supporting details

I started this because I was reasonably confident that this was supported in Edge from the start. Attributes like lang and dir were supported in IE 11 and 10 (tested with the Collector). I couldn't find any mentions of regressions for this feature elsewhere, so I think we can make a more definitive case here for Edge 12.

But then I glanced at the data for api.HTMLElement.dir and it's much more thorough and well tested. I revised this PR to accept the API data as definitive.

Related issues

  • Incited by web-platform-dx/web-features#4533

The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.20.16) found new features shipping in Chromium 157 beta which was released today. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Chrome 157 stable releases on November 3, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on October 29, 2026.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Chromium 157:

HTML setters, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5054329641893888. @tunetheweb can you review this part?

  • api.TrustedHTMLParserOptions (I removed two non-shipping keys here [runScripts and sanitizer], they don't appear in the IDL, cc @tunetheweb)
  • api.TrustedTypePolicy.createParserOptions (new key)

WebTransport reliability attributes, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5094058497277952 (Chromestatus says 158)

  • api.WebTransport.reliability
  • api.WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly_static

WebTransport responseHeaders, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5194104408506368 (Chromestatus says 156)

  • api.WebTransport.responseHeaders

CSS anchor-valid and anchor-visible, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5136123851571200

  • css.properties.position-visibility.anchor-valid
  • css.properties.position-visibility.anchor-visible

CSS text-decoration-inset, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5178263526834176

  • css.properties.text-decoration-inset
  • css.properties.text-decoration-inset.auto

See also https://chromestatus.com/release-notes/157

Some notes:

  • The spec for https://chromestatus.com/feature/5171478175809536 was only merged yesterday, I will have to re-run Collection next week when I have the IDL.
  • The spec for https://chromestatus.com/feature/5172548013916160 is not available yet. I could try to get the IDL manually.
  • https://chromestatus.com/feature/5087964794322944 will need a run on Android.

items.content_html:
Adds webassembly.instructions.ref_null, ref_is_null, ref_func, ref_as_non_null, ref_eq, ref_test and ref_cast.

Summary

Adds compat data for the seven WebAssembly reference instructions (spec "Reference Instructions" section):

  • webassembly.instructions.ref_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_is_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_func
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_as_non_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_eq
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_test
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_cast

Structure follows table_init.json, per @chrisdavidmills’s guidance on the issue.

Test results and supporting details

Versions match the proposal-level features each instruction shipped with, as already recorded in BCD and web-features:

  • ref.null, ref.is_null, ref.func: reference types (webassembly.reference-types): Chrome 96, Firefox 79, Safari 15.1
  • ref.as_non_null: typed function references (webassembly.typedFunctionReferences): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18
  • ref.eq, ref.test, ref.cast: garbage collection (webassembly.garbage-collection): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2Safari 18
  • ref.eq, ref.test, ref.cast: garbage collection (webassembly.garbage-collection): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2

Also cross-checked against https://webassembly.org/features/.

spec_url anchors follow the convention used by table_init and validate against @webref/xref. Tags use the existing wasm-reference-types, wasm-typed-fun-refs and wasm-garbage-collection web-features IDs.

mdn_url is intentionally omitted: the MDN pages are in a companion mdn/content PR, and the URLs can be added once they're live.

npm test: format and lint pass; unit tests 341/341.

Related issues

Relates to mdn/content#37854
items.title: Add WebAssembly reference instructions (ref.*)
